Interface RequestAdmission

public interface RequestAdmission
When a request may proceed while a development launcher reloads the application: a request that arrives while a batch of changes is compiled and applied waits for it, so that it is not answered by a generation about to be replaced, and is never refused while one generation stops and the next starts. A server runtime that holds requests at its own level, below Micronaut's filter chain, such as a servlet container serving servlets of its own, asks it whether to hold a request, and for how long.

A development launcher provides one per process while it runs, current(); outside development mode there is none. The admission is the launcher's: it holds no application context, environment or class of the application, so a server kept across restarts may keep it. Look it up when a server is created or a generation starts, never per request: outside development mode that is one null check.

Admission is granted once the batch is done, or once a restart is about to stop the generation the held requests arrived on: that generation serves them, and those in flight, before it stops, within drainTimeout(). A request a server holds at its own level past that point waits for the next generation.

    • isAdmitted

      boolean isAdmitted()
      Whether a request that arrives now may proceed: true unless a batch of changes is in progress. Cheap, for a gate to check on each request before it allocates anything to hold one.
      Returns:
      True when no batch holds requests

    • whenAdmitted

      CompletionStage<Void> whenAdmitted()
      Completes when a request that arrives now may proceed: at once when no batch is in progress, otherwise once the batch is done or a restart drains the running generation. It always completes normally, and a caller cannot complete it. Holding a request on it is for an asynchronous server; one that blocks a thread per request uses awaitAdmission(Duration).
      Returns:
      The stage

    • awaitAdmission

      default boolean awaitAdmission(Duration timeout) throws InterruptedException
      Blocks until a request that arrives now may proceed, at most for the given time.
      Parameters:
      timeout - How long to wait, usually holdTimeout()
      Returns:
      True when admitted, false when the time ran out first: the request is best answered with a 503 and a Retry-After
      Throws:
      InterruptedException - If the thread is interrupted while it waits
